text.p: - Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek continued Slovenia's diplomatic offensive by visiting his Spanish counterpart Jose Maria Aznar on Thursday. Aznar said Slovenia should enter NATO in the first round of its expansion.
- Government decides to lift electricity prices by 9.8 percent from May 1. The increase would contribute 0.3 percent to May inflation.

- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler met with his Luxembourg counterpart Jacques Poos who said Luxembourg supports Slovenian efforts to join NATO in the first round as well as Slovenia's bid for non-permanent membership to the U.N. Security Council.
- Government decided to send a 20 member medical troop to Albania in the first half of May to take part in the international peace-keeping mission.
- A two-day international conference on Central-Eastern Europe and Euro-Atlantic Security starts in Ljubljana. Some 50 defence experts will participate in the conference.
- Slovenia's Smelt Olimpija won third place in the basketball EuroLeague match on Thursday after beating French Villeurbanne 86-79.
- Listed helth resort operator Terme Catez said 1996 net profit firmed 0.6 percent to 367.2 million tolars ($2.35 million).

- Food producer Kolinska will extend the number of its shares listed on the Ljubljana bourse on May 5. Kolinska will list another 650,977 shares, raising the total to 3,248,048 shares or 91.0 percent of its equity.
